title: ECC spike alert & quarantine automation proposal
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes an automated quarantine workflow for GPU nodes that exhibit sustained spikes in ECC (correctable) error rates. Goal is to reduce noisy on-call churn, protect workloads from progressive memory corruption, and provide a safe, observable containment path that can be reversed without cluster-wide impact.

Context / Motivation:
- Recent trend: intermittent increases in correctable ECC counts followed by downstream computational errors and, in two cases in June, an escalation to uncorrectable errors and driver resets.
- On-call load: manual triage takes 20-60 minutes per event (investigation + scheduling maintenance), causing cascading retries and customer-facing retries on latency-sensitive routes.
- Need a deterministic, reversible action (quarantine + degraded routing) to keep production healthy while SRE and HW teams investigate.

Scope and assumptions:
- Targets: dedicated GPU nodes in serving pools (pools labeled gpu-serving-*). Not intended for training clusters for now.
- Focus on correctable ECC spikes (not immediately fatal) because these provide an early warning window.
- Integration points: Prometheus metrics (nvidia_smi_exporter or dcgm-exporter), Cluster Autoscaler / node controller, Kubernetes taints + cordon/drain, platform routing (Redis/HAProxy) for reroute.

Observed signals (sources):
- Prometheus metric: gpu_ecc_correctable_total{gpu_index, node} (counter)
- kernel/dmesg messages containing "EDAC MC0: CE" or vendor-specific ECC events
- nvidia-smi diagnostics output: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC shows recent increments
- driver reset events: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_model.current \\n- Node-level anomalies: elevated PCIe retries, nvlink flaps (see nvlink_link_errors_total)

Proposed thresholds (starting point, conservative):
- Alert level 1 (informational): single-GPU increases > 50 correctable ECC events in a 1-hour sliding window on a single device. Route to #gpu-observe for visibility.
- Alert level 2 (action recommended): > 200 correctable ECC events in 2 hours on a single GPU OR > 100 events across >=2 GPUs on same host in 2 hours. Notify on-call SRE with runbook link.
- Quarantine trigger (automated): > 500 correctable ECC events in 3 hours on any single GPU OR sustained rate > 0.5 events/min for 10 minutes AND at least one kernel log CE entry in same window.

Automated quarantine actions (high-level):
1) Create an incident ticket (JIRA) annotated with metrics snapshot and recent kernel logs (automation bot).
2) Mark node as "quarantined" in cluster metadata and apply k8s taint: node.kubernetes.io/quarantine=gpu-ecc:NoSchedule.
3) Graceful drain of non-critical pods (if policy allows) with a short eviction grace period (30s) to avoid long stalls. Critical production paths can be routed to fallback pool automatically.
4) Optional power-cycling or soft-reset step only if configured in pool (requires integration with metal API).
5) Attach a runbook link and instructions to the ticket for manual follow-up by hardware team.
6) Post-action snapshot collection: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC, dmesg last 2k lines, /var/log/messages, driver diagnostics (nvidia-bug-report.sh).
7) Escalation: if uncorrectable ECC or driver crash observed post-quarantine, escalate to on-call HW lead and mark node for immediate OOS (Out Of Service).

Manual runbook (short):
- If alert level 2 fires and quarantine did not auto-run (false negative / disabled):
  1) SSH to node, run sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 and sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200.
  2) check Prometheus counters: curl -s <prometheus>/api/v1/query?query=gpu_ecc_correctable_total{node=~\"NODE_NAME\"}
  3) If counts match threshold and kernel shows CE entries, cordon + drain node: kubectl cordon NODE_NAME; kubectl drain NODE_NAME --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30.
  4) Run nvidia-smi -q -d ECC and attach output to incident. Consider running nvidia-bug-report.sh if available.
  5) If node shows repeated CE after reboot or driver upgrade, move to hardware diagnosis and possible RMA.

Automation design details (implementation notes):
- Alerting: Prometheus rule that computes per-GPU rate over sliding windows using increase(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[3h]). Use Alertmanager routing to a new receiver "gpu-quarantine-bot" with a muted window for repeated flaps.
- Quarantine bot: stateless Lambda-like service that calls the cluster API, tagstore, and ticketing API. Idempotent operations only. Rate-limit to one quarantine per node per 24h by default.
- Taint vs Cordon: taint chosen so we can keep the node schedulable by special ops jobs (diagnostics) while preventing normal scheduling. We still cordon+drain when safe.
- Safe drain policy: prefer moving ephemeral work first, keep long-training jobs paused. Add a label on critical pods to skip eviction if necessary.
- Telemetry: attach time-series snapshot (last 6h) to the incident in S3 and link it. Include device-level metrics for GPU 0..N.

Testing plan (staged):
- Canary in dev: run the automation against a fake metric stream, verify taint/cordon behavior on a dev cluster.
- Staging: run against low-traffic serving pool, simulate ECC counts by pushing synthetic metrics and ensure no customer impact.
- Production pilot: enable for a single dedicated serving pool with ops alerting on all auto-steps.

Observability & mitigations for false positives:
- Cross-check with kernel logs: require at least one CE kernel message within window for quarantine to reduce noisy metric-only triggers.
- Require host-level confirmation of multiple GPUs or corroborating PCIe/nvlink counters for single-event spikes.
- Provide a manual "undo quarantine" API for on-call after human review.

Rollback criteria for automation (when to revert quarantine automatically):
- If ECC correctable rate falls and stays below informational threshold for 4 hours and no kernel CE entries in that period, bot can remove taint and mark node as normal.
- If node exhibits uncorrectable ECC or driver crashes, node should remain OOS until certified by hardware team.

Open questions and trade-offs:
- Threshold sensitivity: exact counts are hardware- and workload-dependent. We may need per-cluster or per-hardware-profile thresholds (A100 vs H100).
- Drain policy: aggressive drains reduce client latency risk but can cause extra scheduling churn. Need policy tuning per pool.
- Automated soft-reset: risky if firmware/driver bugs; prefer hands-on for resets unless we have proven safety.
- Ownership: who approves an automatic OOS decision? Propose eng-sre + hw-ops sign-off.

Next steps / action items:
- Review thresholds with Applied ML (Lena) and HW ops (Tomás) — owner: Aisha — due 2025-08-19.
- Prototype Prometheus rule and Alertmanager receiver — owner: Marcus — due 2025-08-26.
- Implement quarantine-bot skeleton and safety checks (idempotency, rate-limits) — owner: SRE infra team — due 2025-09-09.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative to avoid needless disruptions; I expect we’ll iterate thresholds after we see the first few weeks of telemetry.
- We should consider adding a hardware-profile label to nodes (gpu.family=A100/H100) so thresholds can be tuned automatically.
- Saved sample PromQLs: 
  - per-GPU 3h increase: increase(gpu_ecc_correctable_total{node=\"NODE\",gpu_index=\"0\"}[3h])
  - per-node aggregate in 1h: sum(increase(gpu_ecc_correctable_total{node=\"NODE\"}[1h])) by (node)

Appendix (commands & quick snippets):
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC\\- shows ECC counters per device.
- sudo dmesg | grep -i -E "EDAC|CE|uncorrectable|NVRM"
- kubectl taint nodes NODE_NAME node.kubernetes.io/quarantine=gpu-ecc:NoSchedule --overwrite
- kubectl uncordon NODE_NAME

End of doc.
